υἱός.sd: a "son" (sometimes of animals), used very widely of immediate, remote or figuratively, kinship
υἱός.as:
υἱός, -οῦ, ὁ, [in LXX very freq. and nearly always for בֵּן, Ge 4:17, al.; for בַּר, Da LXX TH 7:13, al.; etc. ;],
a son;
1. in the ordinary sense: Mt 10:37, Mk 9:17, Lk 1:13, al. mult.; omitted with the art. of origin (WM, § 30, 3; Bl., §35, 2), τὸν τοῦ Ἰεσσαί, Ac 13:22(LXX); also c. gen. anarth. (cl.), Σώπατρος Πύρρου Βεροιαῖος, Ac 20:4; c. adj., προτότοκος, Lk 2:7; μονογένης, Lk 7:12; opp. to νόθος, He 12:8; in a wider sense, of posterity: ὁ υἱ. Δαυΐδ, of the Messiah (cf. Dalman, Words, 316 ff.; DCG, ii, 653f .), Mt 22:42, 45Mk 12:35, 37Lk 20:41, 44 al.; υἱοὶ Ἰσραήλ, (cf. υἷες Ἀχαιῶν, Hom., Il., i, 162, al.), Mt 27:9, Ac 9:15, al.
2. Metaph.;
(a) as belonging to, being connected with or having the quality of that which follows (a usage mainly due to translation from a Semitic original; cf. Deiss., BS, 161ff.; Dalman, Words, 115 f.; DCG, ii, 652f.): τ. πονμροῦ (διαβόλου), Mt 13:38, Ac 13:10; τ. νυμφῶνος (v.s. νυμφών), Mt 9:15, Mk 2:19, al.; τ. φωτός (Lft., Notes, 74), Lk 16:8, Jo 12:36, I Th 5:5; τ. εἰρήνης, Lk 10:6; γεέννης, Mt 23:15; τ. ἀπωλείας, Jo 17:12, II Th 2:3; τ. αἰῶνος τούτου, Lk 16:820:34; τ. ἀπειθειάς, Eph 2:25:6; βροντῆς, Mk 3:17; τ. ἀναστάσεως, Lk 20:36; παρακλήσεως, Ac 4:36; τ. προφητῶν κ. τ. διαθήκης, Ac 3:25;
(b)υἱὸς τ. θεοῦ (cf. Dalman, Words, 268 ff.; Deiss., BS, 166 f.; DB, iv, 570 ff.; DCG, ii, 654 ff.), of men, as partakers of the Divine nature and of the life to come: Mt 5:9, Lk 20:36, Ro 8:149:26, al.; υἱοὶ (κ. θυγατέρες) τ. ὑψίστου, Lk 6:35, II Co 6:18; in an unique sense of Jesus, Mt 4:38:2928:19, Mk 3:4, Lk 4:41, Jo 9:3511:27, al.; ὁ Χριστὸς ὁ υἱ. τ. θεοῦ ζῶντος (τ. εὐλογητοῦ), Mt 16:16, Mk 14:61;
(c)(ὁ) υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου (in LXX for Heb. בּן אדם, Aram, בּר אנשׁ; cf. Dalman, Words, 234 ff.; DB, iv, 579 ff.; DCG, ii, 659 ff.; Westc., St. John, i, 74 ff.; other reff. in Swete, Mk, 2:10), based on the Aram. of Da 7:13, where the phrase, like the corresponding Heb. (as in Ps 8:5), means a man, one of the species, and indicates the human appearance of the person in question. It is used of the Messiah in Enoch, c. 46, §1-4, also in II Es 13:3, 12 , al. Our Lord first makes the phrase a title, using the def. art. It seems to combine the ideas of his true humanity and representative character. Exc. in Ac 7:56 and (anarth.) Re 1:1314:14, it is used of Jesus only by himself: Mt 8:20, Mk 2:10, Lk 5:24, Jo 1:52, al.

ὑπό.sd: under, i.e. (with the genitive case) of place (beneath), or with verbs (the agency or means, through); (with the accusative case) of place (whither (underneath) or where (below) or time (when (at))
ὑπό.kj: among, by, from, in, of, under, with
ὑπό.as:
ὑπό (before smooth breathing ὑπ’, Mt 8:9b, Lk 7:8b; before rough breathing ὑφ’, Ro 3:9; on the neglect of elision in Mt, Lk, ll. c.a, Ga 3:22, v. WH, App., 146; Tdf., Pr., iv),
prep. c. gen., dat. (not in NT), acc.
I. C. gen., primarily of place, under, hence, metaph., of the efficient cause, by: after passive verbs, c. gen. pers., Mt 1:22, Mk 1:5, Lk 2:18, Jo 14:21, Ac 4:11, I Co 1:11, He 3:4, al.; c. gen. rei, Mt 8:24, Lk 7:24, Ro 3:21, al.; with neut. verbs and verbs with pass. meaning, Mt 17:12, Mk 5:26, I Co 10:9, 10I Th 2:14, al.
II. C. acc., under;
1. of motion: Mt 5:158:8, Mk 4:21, Lk 13:34; hence, metaph., of subjection, Ro 7:14, I Co 15:27, Ga 3:22, I Pe 5:6, al.
2. Of position: Jo 1:49, Ac 4:12, Ro 3:13, I Co 10:1, al.; hence, metaph., under, subject to, Mt 8:9, Ro 3:9, I Co 9:20, Ga 4:5, al.
3. Of time, about: Ac 5:21.
III. In composition: under (ὑποδέω), hence, of subjection (ὑποτάσσω), compliance (ὑπακούω), secrecy (ὑποβάλλω), diminution (ὑποπνέω).

ὕπνος.der: from an obsolete primary (perhaps akin to G5259 (ὑπό) through the idea of subsilience);
ὕπνος.as:
ὕπνος, -ου, ὁ
[in LXX for שֵׁנָה, חֲלוֹם, etc. ;]
sleep: Mt 1:24, Lk 9:32, Jo 11:13, Ac 20:9; metaph., Ro 13:11.†

ὑποδείκνυμι.long: I indicate, intimate, suggest, show, prove.
ὑποδείκνυμι.sd: to exhibit under the eyes, i.e. (figuratively) to exemplify (instruct, admonish)
ὑποδείκνυμι.as:
ὑπο-δείκνυμι
[in LXX for נָגַד hi., etc. ;]
1.to show secretly.
2.to show by tracing out; hence, generally, to teach, make known: c. dat. pers., Lk 6:4712:5, Ac 9:16; id. c. inf., Mt 3:7, Lk 3:7; seq., ὅτι, Ac 20:35.†

ὕδωρ.sd: water (as if rainy) literally or figuratively
ὕδωρ.as:
ὕδωρ gen., ὕδατος, τό,
[in LXX chiefly for מַיִם ;]
water: Mt 3:16, Mk 1:10, Lk 7:44, Jo 4:7, Ja 3:12, Re 8:10, al.; pl., Mt 14:28, 29, Jo 3:23, Re 1:15, al.; βαπτίζειν (ἐν) ὕδατι, Mt 3:11, Mk 1:8, Jo 1:26, al.; τ. λουτρὸν τοῦ ὕ., Eph 5:26; opp. to οἴνος, Jo 2:94:46; αἷμα, Jo 19:34, He 9:19, I Jo 5:6, 8, Mt 17:15, Mk 9:22; πνεῦμα, Jo 1:26, 31, 33; πνεῦμα καὶ πῦρ, Mt 3:11, Lk 3:16; ἐξ ὕ. κ. πνεύματος γεννηθῆναι, Jo 3:5; metaph., of divine truth and grace (τ.) ὕ. (τ.) ζῶν, Jo 4:10, 11 (cf. ib. 13-15,); τ. ὕ. τ. ζωῆς, of spiritual refresh­ment, Re 21:622:1, 17

ὑπόδημα.sd: something bound under the feet, i.e. a shoe or sandal
ὑπόδημα.as:
ὑπόδημα, -τος, τό
(< ὑποδέω), [in LXX for נָעַל ;]
a sole bound under the foot, a sandal: Mt 3:1110:10, Mk 1:7, Lk 3:1610:415:2222:35, Jo 1:27; τ. ποδῶν, Ac 7:33(LXX)Ac 13:25.†
SYN.: σανδάλιον, q.v

ὕστερος.der: comparative from G5259 (ὑπό) (in the sense of behind);
ὕστερος.as:
ὕστερος, -α, -ον
[in LXX for אַחֲרוֹן and cogn. forms ;]
latter, later: ἐν ὑ. καιροῖς, I Ti 4:1 (on the reading ὁ ὕ., WH, for ὁ πρῶτος, v. WH, App., in l.). Neut., τὸ ὕ., used adverbially instead of ὑστέρως, afterwards, later: Mt 4:221:29, 32, 3725:1126:60, Mk 16:14, Lk 20:32, Jo 13:36, He 12:11; c. gen., Mt 22:27.†

ὑψηλός.as:
ὑψηλός, -ή, -όν
[in LXX chiefly for בָּמָה, also for בָּמָה, רוּם, etc. ;]
high, lofty: ὄρος, Mt 4:817:1, Mk 9:2, Re 21:10; τεῖχος, ib. 12; μετὰ βραχίονος., fig., Ac 13:17 (cf. Ex 6:6, al); pl., ὑψηλά, of heaven (Ps 92 (93):4, Is 33:5, al.), He 1:3; compar., ὑψηλότερος τ. οὐρανῶν, He 7:26. Metaph: Lk 16:15; ὑψηλὰ φρονεῖν, Ro 11:2012:16, I Ti 6:17 (WH, txt., ὑψηλοφρονείν).†

ὑπάγω.long: I go away, depart, begone, die.
ὑπάγω.sd: to lead (oneself) under, i.e. withdraw or retire (as if sinking out of sight), literally or figuratively
ὑπάγω.as:
ὑπ-άγω
[in LXX: Ex 14:21 (הָלַךְ hi.), elsewhere only as v.l., To 8:21, al. ;]
a word of the vulgar language, in Pres. and impf. only (Bl., § 53, 1).
I. Trans.
1.to lead or bring under, subdue (Hom., Hdt., al.; Ex, l.c..
2.to lead on slowly (Hdt., Xen., al.).
II. Intrans., to go slowly away, withdraw oneself, depart (so less freq. in cl.; Thuc., Eur., al.): absol., Mt 8:3213:44, Mk 6:33, Lk 8:4217:14, Jo 6:678:211:4414:5, 2818:8; οἱ ἐρχόμενοι κ. οἱ ὑπάγοντες, Mk 6:31; ὑπῆγον κ. ἐπίστευον, Jo 12:11; ἵνα ὑπαγῆτε κ. καρπὸν ψέρητε, Jo 15:16; opp. to ἔρχεσθαι, Jo 3:88:14; imperat., ὕπαγε, Mt 4:108:1320:14, Mk 2:9 T, 7:2910:52; εἰς εἰρήνην (ἐν εἰ.), Mk 5:34, Ja 2:16; id. prefixed to another imperat. (Bl., § 79, 4), Mt 5:348:418:1519:2121:2827:6528:10, Mk 1:4410:2116:7, Jo 4:169:7, Re 10:8; with καί inserted, Re 16:1; euphemistically, of death, Mt 26:24, Mk 14:21; c. adv.: ποῦ (q.v.), Jo 12:3514:516:5, I Jo 2:11; ὅπου (q.v.), Jo 8:21, 2213:33, 3614:4, Re 14:4; ἐκεῖ, Jo 11:8; c. prep.: πρός, Jo 7:3313:316:5, 10, 17; εἰς, Mt 9:620:4, 7, Mk 2:1111:214:13, Lk 19:30, Jo 6:217:39:1111:31, Re 13:1017:8, 11; εἰς . . . πρός, Mt 26:18, Mk 5:19; ἐπί, Lk 12:58; μετά, Mt 5:41; ὀπίσω, Mt 16:23, Mk 8:33; c. inf., Jo 21:3.†

ὑπηρέτης.long: a servant, an attendant, (a) an officer, lictor, (b) an attendant in a synagogue, (c) a minister of the gospel.
ὑπηρέτης.sd: an under-oarsman, i.e. (generally) subordinate (assistant, sexton, constable)
ὑπηρέτης.der: from G5259 (ὑπό) and a derivative of (to row);
ὑπηρέτης.as:
ὑπηρέτης, -ου, ὁ
(< ὑπό + ἐρέτης, a rower) [in LXX: Pr 14:35 (עֶבֶד), Wi 6:4, al. ;]
prop., an under rower; hence, generally, a servant, attendant, minister: of a magistrate's attendant, Mt 5:25; of officers of the Synagogue or Sanhedrin, Mt 26:58, Mk 14:54, 65, Lk 4:20, Jo 7:32, 45, 4618:3, 12, 2219:6, Ac 5:22, 26; of the attendants of kings, οἱ ὑ. οἱ ἑμοίJo 18:36; of Christian ministers, Ac 13:526:16; ὑπηρέται λόγου, Lk 1:2; Χριστοῦ, I Co 4:1; δοῦλοι κ. ὑ., Jo 18:18.†
SYN.: v.s. διάκονος

ὑποπόδιον.sd: something under the feet, i.e. a foot-rest (figuratively)
ὑποπόδιον.der: neuter of a compound of G5259 (ὑπό) and G4228 (πούς);
ὑποπόδιον.as:
† ὑποπόδιον, -ου, τό
(< ὑπό, πούς), [in LXX: Ps 98 (99):5109 (110):1, Is 66:1, La 2:1 (הֲדֹם) * ;]
a footstool (= cl. θρᾶνος): Ja 2:3; metaph., Mt 5:35, Mk 12:36 (ὑποκάτω, WH, R, mg.), Lk 20:43, Ac 2:357:49, He 1:1310:13 (all, except Mt, l.c., from LXX, Ps 109 (110):1, Is 66:1) (for exx., v. Deiss., BS, 223).†

ὑπέρ.long: gen: in behalf of; acc: above.
ὑπέρ.sd: "over", i.e. (with the genitive case) of place, above, beyond, across, or causal, for the sake of, instead, regarding; with the accusative case superior to, more than
ὑπέρ.kj: (+ exceeding, abundantly) above, in (on) behalf of, beyond, by, + very chiefest, concerning, exceeding (above, -ly), for, + very highly, more (than), of, over, on the part of, for sake of, in stead, than, to(-ward), very
ὑπέρ.as:
ὑπέρ (when following subst.—poët.—ὕπερ; so as adv., II Co 11:23),
prep. c. gen., acc.
I. C. gen., primarily of place (rest or motion), over, above, across, beyond, hence, metaph.,
1.for, on behalf of: of prayer, Mt 5:44, Ac 8:24, Ro 10:1, Ja 5:16, al.; of laying down life, Jo 10:11, Ro 9:3, al.; esp. of Christ giving his life for man's redemption, Mk 14:24, Jo 10:15, Ac 21:13, Ro 5:6-8, al.; opp. to κατά, Mk 9:40, Lk 9:50, Ro 8:31.
2. Causal, for, because of, for the sake of: c. gen. pers., Ac 5:41, Ro 1:5, Phl 1:29, II Co 12:10, al.; c. gen. rei, Jo 11:4, Ro 15:8, II Co 1:6, al.
3. = ἀντί (v. M, Pr., 105), for, instead of, in the name of : I Co 15:29, II Co 5:15, 21Ga 3:13, Col 1:7, Phm 13 (cf. Field, Notes, 225).
4. In more colourless sense, = περί (M, Pr., l.c.), for, concerning, with regard to: Ro 9:27, II Co 1:68:2312:8, Phl 1:7, II Th 2:1, al.

II. C. acc., primarily of place, over, beyond, across, hence, metaph., of measure or degree in excess, above, beyond, over, more than: Mt 10:24, 37Lk 6:40, Ac 26:13, I Co 10:13, II Co 1:8, Eph 1:223:20, Phm 16, al.; after comparatives = than (Jg 11:25, al.), Lk 16:8, He 4:12.

III. As adv. (v. supr. ad init.), more: ὕπερ ἐγώ, I more, II Co 11:23; in compounds, v.s. ὑπεράνω, ὑπερλίαν, ὑπερπερισσῶς.

IV. In composition: over (ὑπεραίρω), beyond (ὑπερβάλλω), more (ὐπερνικάω), on behalf of (ὐπερεντυγχάνω).

ὑποκριτής.long: (lit: a stage-player), a hypocrite, dissembler, pretender.
ὑποκριτής.sd: an actor under an assumed character (stage-player), i.e. (figuratively) a dissembler ("hypocrite"
ὑποκριτής.as:
ὑπο-κριτής, -οῦ, ὁ
(< ὑποκρίνομαι, q.v.) [in LXX Jb 34:3036:13 (חָנֵף) * ;]
1.one who answers, an interpreter (Plat.).
2.a stage player, actor (Plut., Xen., al.). Metaph. (in LXX and NT), a pretender, dissembler, hypocrite: Mt 6:2, 5, 167:515:722:1823:13-1524:51, Mk 7:6Lk 6:4212:5613:15.†

ὑπακούω.long: I listen, hearken to, obey, answer.
ὑπακούω.sd: to hear under (as a subordinate), i.e. to listen attentively; by implication, to heed or conform to a command or authority
ὑπακούω.as:
ὑπακούω
[in LXX: chiefly for שָׁמַע ;]
vto listen, attend, hence,
(a)to answer a knock at a door (Plat., Xen., al.): Ac 12:13;
(b)to attend to, submit to, obey (Hdt., Thuc., al.): absol., Phl 2:12; c. inf., He 11:8; c. dat. pers. (Plat., al.; but more freq. c. gen.), Mt 8:27, Mk 1:274:41, Lk 8:2517:6, Ro 6:16, Eph 6:1, 5, Col 3:20, 22, He 5:9, I Pe 3:6; c. dat. rei, Ac 6:7, Ro 6:1210:16, II Th 1:83:14; seq. εἰς (by attraction, for dat.; v. ICC, in l.), Ro 6:17.†

ὑπαντάω.sd: to go opposite (meet) under (quietly), i.e. to encounter, fall in with
ὑπαντάω.der: from G5259 (ὑπό) and a derivative of G473 (ἀντί);
ὑπαντάω.as:
ὑπ-αντάω, -ῶ
[in LXX: Da LXX 10:14 (קָרָה), Si 9:3, al. ;]
to go to meet, meet: c. dat. pers. (v. M, Pr., 64), Mt 8:2828:9, Mk 5:2, Lk 8:2717:12 (ἀπ-, WH, txt.), Jo 4:5111:20, 3012:18, Ac 16:16; of meeting in battle, Lk 14:31.†

ὑπάντησις.sd: an encounter or concurrence (with G1519 (εἰς) for infinitive, in order to fall in with)
ὑπάντησις.as:
† ὑπ-άντησις, -εως, ἡ
(< ὑπαντάω), [in LXX: Jg 11:34, εἰς ὑ. (לִקְרָאת), etc. ;]
a going to meet: εἰς ὑ. (v. M, Pr., 14 n), Mt 8:3425:1, Jo 12:13.†

ὑπομένω.long: (a) I remain behind, (b) I stand my ground, show endurance, (c) I endure, bear up against, persevere.
ὑπομένω.sd: to stay under (behind), i.e. remain; figuratively, to undergo, i.e. bear (trials), have fortitude, persevere
ὑπομένω.kj: abide, endure, (take) patient(-ly), suffer, tarry behind
ὑπομένω.as:
ὑπο-μένω
[in LXX chiefly for קָוָה, also for יָחַל hi., etc. ;]
1. in-trans., to stay behind: seq. ἐν, Lk 2:43; ἐκεῖ, Ac 17:14.
2. Trans.,
(a) c. acc, to await, wait for: Ro 8:24 (Hom., Hdt., Xen., al.);
(b) of things, to bear patiently, endure: absol., Mt 10:2224:13, Mk 13:13, II Ti 2:12, Ja 5:11, I Pe 2:20; τ. θλίψει (dat. of circumstance), Ro 12:12; seq. εἰς, He 12:7; c. acc rei, I Co 13:7, II Ti 2:10, He 10:3212:2,3, Ja 1:12.†
SYN.: μακροθυμέω (v.s. ὑπομονή)

ὑψόω.long: (a) I raise on high, lift up, (b) I exalt, set on high.
ὑψόω.as:
ὑψόω, -ῶ
(< ὕψος), [in LXX chiefly for רוּם, also for גָּבַהּ, נָשָׂא, etc. ;]
to lift or raise up: c. acc, Jo 3:148:2812:32, 34; ἕως τ. οὐρανοῦ, fig., pass., Mt 11:23, Lk 10:15. Metaph., to exalt, uplift: Ac 2:335:31, II Co 11:7, Ja 4:10, I Pe 5:6; opp. to ταπεινῶ, Lk 1:52; ἑαυτόν, Mt 23:12, Lk 4:1118:14 (cf. ὑπερ-υψόω).†

ὑγιής.sd: healthy, i.e. well (in body); figuratively, true (in doctrine)
ὑγιής.as:
ὑγιής, -ές, acc., ὑγιῆ (Attic usually -ιᾶ),
[in LXX for חַי, etc. ;]
sound, whole, healthy: Mt 12:1315:31, Jo 5:[4], 6, 9, 11, 14, 157:23, Ac 4:10; seq. ἀπό, Mk 5:34; of words, opinions, etc. (as in cl.), metaph., λόγος, Tit 2:8.†

ὑστερέω.g: I am lacking, fall short, suffer need
ὑστερέω.long: I fall behind, am lacking, fall short, suffer need, am inferior to.
ὑστερέω.sd: to be later, i.e. (by implication) to be inferior; generally, to fall short (be deficient)
ὑστερέω.kj: come behind (short), be destitute, fail, lack, suffer need, (be in) want, be the worse
ὑστερέω.as:
ὑστερέω, -ῶ
(< ὕστερος), [in LXX for חָסֵר, חָדַל etc. ;]
to come late, be behind (opp. to προτερέω, φθάνω; c. gen. rei, for; c. gen. pers., later than).
Metaph.,
1. of persons,
(a) absol., to come short, fail: He 4:1; seq. ἀπό, 12:15.;
(b) c. gen. pers., to come short of, be inferior to: II Co 11:5; οὐδέν (in nothing, in no respect), ib. 12:11;
(c) with reference to things, to come short (of), be in want (of): c. acc rei, Mt 19:20 (Si 51:24); c. gen. rei, Lk 22:35; so mid. (Diod., FlJ), Ro 3:23; absol., to be in want, suffer want, Lk 15:14, I Co 8:8, II Co 11:8, He 11:37 (Si 11:11); opp. to περισσεύειν, Phl 4:12; seq. ἐν, I Co 1:7.
2. Of things,
(a)to fail, be lacking: Jo 2:3; c. acc pers. (v. Swete, in l.; Mozley, Ps., 42), Mk 10:21;
(b)to be inferior: mid., I Co 12:24 (cf. ἀφ-υστερέω).†

ὑπάρχω.g: I am, exist, am in possession
ὑπάρχω.long: I begin, am, exist, am in possession.
ὑπάρχω.sd: to begin under (quietly), i.e. come into existence (be present or at hand); expletively, to exist (as copula or subordinate to an adjective, participle, adverb or preposition, or as an auxiliary to a principal (verb)
ὑπάρχω.as:
ὑπάρχω
[in LXX for הָיָה, יֵשׁ, לוּן, etc.; τ. ὑπάρχοντα for מִקְנֶה, רְכוּשׁ, etc. ;]
1.to begin, make a beginning (Hom., Hdt., al.).
2.to be in existence, be ready, be at hand (Hdt., Thuc., al.): Ac 19:4027:12, 21; seq. ἐν, Ac 28:18.
3.to be, prop, expressing continuance of an antecedent state or condition (cf. Gifford, Incarnation, 11 ff.; MM, xxv): c. nom. pred., Lk 8:419:48, Ac 4:347:558:1616:319:3621:20, I Co 7:2612:22, Ja 2:15, II Pe 3:11; ptcp. c. pred., Lk 16:1423:50, Ac 2:303:217:2422:3, Ro 4:19, I Co 11:7, II Co 8:1712:16, Ga 1:142:14; pl., Lk 11:13, Ac 16:20, 3717:29, II Pe 2:19; seq. ἐν, c. dat. rei, Lk 7:2516:23, Ac 5:410:12, I Co 11:18, Phl 3:20; ἐν μορφῇ θεοῦ ὑπάρχων (R, mg., being originally), Phl 2:6; ἐν, c. dat. pers., (among), I Co 11:18; μακρὰν ἀπό, Ac 17:27; πρὸς τ. σωτηρίας, Ac 27:34.
4.to belong to (Thuc., Xen., al.): c. dat. pers., Ac 3:64:3728:7, II Pe 1:8; τὰ ὑπάρχοντα, one's belongings, possessions: c. dat. pers., Lk 8:312:15, Ac 4:32; c. gen. pers., Mt 19:2124:4725:14, Lk 11:2112:33, 4414:3316:119:8, I Co 13:3, He 10:34 (cf. προ-υπάρχω).†

ὑποζύγιον.g: a beast of burden, an ass or mule
ὑποζύγιον.long: a beast of burden, an ass or mule.
ὑποζύγιον.sd: an animal under the yoke (draught-beast), i.e. (specially), a donkey
ὑποζύγιον.der: neuter of a compound of G5259 (ὑπό) and G2218 (ζυγός);
ὑποζύγιον.as:
ὑπο-ζύγιος, -α, -ον
[in LXX for חֲמוֹר ;]
under the yoke; as subst., τὸ ζ. (Hdt., al.), a beast of burden; colloq., an ass (v. Deiss., BS, 160 f.), and so always in LXX and NT: Mt 21:5(LXX), II Pe 2:16.†

ὕψιστος.sd: highest, i.e. (masculine singular) the Supreme (God), or (neuter plural) the heavens
ὕψιστος.der: superlative from the base of G5311 (ὕψος);
ὕψιστος.as:
ὕψιστος, -η, -ον superlat., without positive in use, in cl. chiefly poët. (Æsch., Soph., al.),
[in LXX chiefly for עֶלְיוֹן, also for מָרוֹם, etc. ;]
highest, most high: of place, τὰ ὕ. (of the heavens), Mt 21:9, Mk 11:10, Lk 2:1419:38 (cf. Jos 16:19, Is 57:15); of God (in cl., of Zeus; Pind., Æsch., al.), ὕ., Lk 1:32, 35, 766:35 (as freq. in Si 4:10, al.); ὁ ὕ., Ac 7:48; ὁ θεὸς ὁ ὕ., Mk 5:7, Lk 8:28, Ac 16:17, He 7:1 (cf. Ge 14:18).†

ὑβρίζω.as:
ὑβρίζω
(< ὕβρις), [in LXX for גֵּאֶה, etc. ;]
1. intrans., to wax wanton, run riot.
2. Trans., to outrage, insult, treat insolently: c. acc pers., Mt 22:6, Lk 11:4518:32, Ac 14:5, I Th 2:2.†

ὑποκάτω.as:
ὑπο-κάτω comp. adv. (v. M, Pr., 99),
[in LXX chiefly for תַּחַת ;]
below, under: as prep. c. gen., Mt 22:44, Mk 6:117:2812:36 (Rec., R, txt., ὑποπόδιον, as in LXX), Lk 8:16, Jo 1:51, He 2:8(LXX), Re 5:3, 136:912:1.†

ὑπόκρισις.long: (lit: stage-playing), a response, answer, hypocrisy, dissembling.
ὑπόκρισις.sd: acting under a feigned part, i.e. (figuratively) deceit ("hypocrisy")
ὑπόκρισις.as:
** ὑπό-κρισις, -εως, ἡ
(< ὑποκρίνομαι, q.v.) [in LXX: II Mac 6:25 * ;]
1. a reply, answer (Hdt.).
2. play-acting (Arist., Polyb., al.). Metaph., pretence, hypocrisy: Mt 23:28, Mk 12:15, Lk 12:1, Ga 2:13, I Ti 4:2, I Pe 2:1 (Polyb., Pss Sol 4:7).†

ὑμνέω.long: I sing, sing hymns to, praise.
ὑμνέω.sd: to hymn, i.e. sing a religious ode; by implication, to celebrate (God) in song
ὑμνέω.as:
ὑμνέω, -ῶ
(< ὕμνος) [in LXX for הָלַל pi., שִׁיר, יָדָה hi., etc. ;]
1. trans., c. acc pers. (in cl. also c. acc. rei), to sing to, laud, sing to the praise of: Ac 16:25, He 2:12.
2. Intrans., to sing: in LXX and NT, of singing hymns and praises to God (Ps 64 (65):13, al.), Mt 26:30, Mk 14:26 (v. Swete, in l.).†

ὑποδέομαι.long: (lit: I bind under), mid: I put on my feet, pass: I am shod.
ὑποδέομαι.sd: to bind under one's feet, i.e. put on shoes or sandals
ὑποδέομαι.as:
ὑπο-δέω
[in LXX: II Ch 28:15, Ez 16:10 (נָעַל) * ;]
to bind under, esp. of foot gear. Most freq. in mid, and pass. c. acc;
(a) of the foot, ὑποδησάμενοι τ. πόδας, your feet shod: Eph 6:15;
(b) of that which is put on, σανδάλια: Mk 6:9, Ac 12:8.†

ὑπερηφανία.as:
ὑπερηφανία, -ας, ἡ
(< ὑπερήφανος, q.v.), [in LXX chiefly for גָּאוֹן and cogn. forms ;]
haughtiness, arrogance, disdain:Mk 7:22 (Plat., Xen.).†

ὑπολήνιον.long: a wine-vat, pit under the wine-press dug in the ground.
ὑπολήνιον.sd: vessel or receptacle under the press, i.e. lower wine-vat
ὑπολήνιον.der: neuter of a presumed compound of G5259 (ὑπό) and G3025 (ληνός);
ὑπολήνιον.as:
† ὑπολήνιον, -ου, τό
(< ὑπό, ληνός), [in LXX: Jl 3 (4):13, Ha 2:17(16), Za 14:10, Is 16:10 (יֶקֶב) * ;]
a vessel or trough beneath a winepress to receive the juice (RV, a pit for the winepress)Mk 12:1 (v. Swete, in l, and cf. ληνός).†

ὑστέρησις.as:
**† ὑστέρησις, -εως, ἡ
(< ὑστερέω), [in Aq.: Jb 30:3 * ;]
need, want: opp. to τὸ περισσεῦον, Mk 12:44; καθ’ ὑ., Phl 4:11 (eccl.).†

ὑπερήφανος.as:
ὑπερήφανος, -ον
(< ὑπέρ, φαίνομαι, c. η pleonast., v. Kühner3, I, 189) [in LXX for זֵד, גֵּאֶה, לוּץ, etc. ;]
showing oneself above others;
(a) in good sense (Plat., al.), pre-eminent, splendid;
(b) more freq. in had sense, and so always in Scr., arrogant, haughty, disdainful (v. Westc. Epp. Jo., 65b): Ro 1:30, II Ti 3:2; διανοίᾳ καρδίας, Lk 1:51; opp. to ταπεινός (as in Pr 3:34), Ja 4:6, I Pe 5:5(LXX).†
SYN.: ἀλαζών, ὑβριστής, v. Tr., Syn., § xxix

ὑποστρέφω.sd: to turn under (behind), i.e. to return (literally or figuratively)
ὑποστρέφω.kj: come again, return (again, back again), turn back (again)
ὑποστρέφω.as:
ὑπο-στρέφω
[in LXX chiefly for שׁוּב ],
1. trans., to turn back or about (Hom.).
2. Intrans., to turn back, return: Lk 2:20, 438:37, 409:1010:1717:1519:1223:48, 56, Ac 8:28; c. inf., Lk 17:18; seq.. διά, Ac 20:3; εἰς, Lk 1:562:454:147:108:3911:2424:33, 52, Ac 1:128:2513:13, 3414:2121:622:1723:32, Ga 1:17; ἀπό, Lk 4:124:9, He 7:1; ἐκ, Ac 12:25, II Pe 2:21.†

ὕψος.sd: elevation, i.e. (abstractly) altitude, (specially), the sky, or (figuratively) dignity
ὕψος.as:
ὕψος, -ους, τό
[in LXX for קוֹמָה, מָרוֹם, etc. ;]
height: Eph 3:18Ja 1:9, Re 21:16; of heaven (EV, on high), ἐξ ὕ., Lk 1:7824:49; εἰς ὕ., Eph 4:8(LXX)†

ὑποτάσσω.long: I place under, subject to; mid, pass: I submit, put myself into subjection.
ὑποτάσσω.kj: be under obedience (obedient), put under, subdue unto, (be, make) subject (to, unto), be (put) in subjection (to, under), submit self unto
ὑποτάσσω.as:
ὑπο-τάσσω
[in LXX for דָבַר hi., דָּמַם, שׂוּם, שִׁית, etc. ;]
1. as a military term, to place or rank under (Polyb.).
2.to subject, put in subjection: I Co 15:27, Phl 3:21, He 2:5, 8; pass., Ro 8:20, I Co 15:27, 28, I Pe 3:22, Eph 1:22. Mid., to subject oneself, obey: absol., Ro 13:5, I Co 14:34; c. dat. pers., Lk 2:5110:17, 20, Ro 8:710:313:1, I Co 14:3215:28 (ὑποταγήσεται; cf. M, Pr., 163), ib. 16:16, Eph 5:21, 22 (T, WH, txt., R, om.), ib. 24, Col 3:18, Tit 2:5, 93:1, He 12:9, I Pe 2:183:13:55:5; imperat., Ja 4:7, I Pe 2:135:5.†

ὑποχωρέω.long: I withdraw, retire, go back, retreat.
ὑποχωρέω.sd: to vacate down, i.e. retire quietly
ὑποχωρέω.as:
ὑπο-χωρέω
[in LXX: Jg 20:37 B (—), Si 13:9, II Mac 12:12 * ;]
to go back, retire: seq. ἐν, Lk 5:16; seq. εἰς, Lk 9:10.†

ὑγιαίνω.long: I am well, am in good health; I am right, reasonable, sound, pure, uncorrupted.
ὑγιαίνω.sd: to have sound health, i.e. be well (in body); figuratively, to be uncorrupt (true in doctrine)
ὑγιαίνω.kj: be in health, (be safe and) sound, (be) whole(-some)
ὑγιαίνω.as:
ὑγιαίνω
(< ὑγιής), [in LXX chiefly for שָׁלוֹם, and freq. in To ;]
to be sound, healthy, in good health: Lk 5:317:1015:27, III Jo 2. In Past. Epp. (as also in cl.) metaph., ὑ. ἐν τ. πίστει, Tit 1:13 ; τ. πίστει, τ. ἀγάπῃ, τ. ὑπομονῇ, Tit 2:2; ἡ ὑγιαίνουσα διδασκαλία, I Ti 1:10, II Ti 4:3, Tit 1:92:1 ; λόγοι ὑγιαίνοντες, I Ti 6:3 , II Ti 1:13.†

ὑμέτερος.as:
ὑμέτερος, -α, -ον
poss. pron. of second pers. pl. (= emphasized gen., ὑμῶν),
your, yours: Jo 7:68:1715:20, Ac 27:34, Ro 11:31, I Co 16:17, II Co 8:8, Ga 6:13; as pred., Lk 6:20; τὸ ὑ., as subst., opp. to τ. ἀλλότριον, Lk 16:12 (WH, txt., R, mg., ἡμέτερον); objectively, ὑ. καύχησις, my glorying in you, I Co 15:31.†

ὑπερεκχύννομαι.g: I pour out so that it overflows
ὑπερεκχύννομαι.long: I pour out so that it overflows.
ὑπερεκχύννομαι.sd: to pour out over, i.e. (passively) to overflow
ὑπερεκχύννομαι.der: from G5228 (ὑπέρ) and the alternate form of G1632 (ἐκχέω);
ὑπερεκχύννομαι.as:
*† ὑπερ-εκ-χύννω
(Rec. -ύνω), late form of -χέω
to pour out over. Pass., to overflow, run over: Lk 6:38 (not elsewhere).†

ὑπολαμβάνω.g: I take up, receive, answer, suppose, welcome
ὑπολαμβάνω.long: (a) I take up, (b) I welcome, entertain, (c) I answer, (d) I suppose, imagine.
ὑπολαμβάνω.sd: to take from below, i.e. carry upward; figuratively, to take up, i.e. continue a discourse or topic; mentally, to assume (presume)
ὑπολαμβάνω.as:
ὑπο-λαμβάνω
[in LXX: Jb 2:44:1 and freq. (עָנָה), Ps 47 (48):9 (דָּמָה pi.), To 6:17, Wi 17:2, III Mac 3:8, 11, al. ;]
1.to take or bear up (by supporting from beneath): c. acc pers., Ac 1:9.
2.to receive, welcome, entertain (Xen.): III Jo 8.
3.to catch up in speech (Hdt., al.; Jb, ll. c.): Lk 10:30.
4. Of mental action, to assume, suppose (Xen., al.; To, Wis, III Mac, ll. c.): Ac 2:15; seq. ὅτι (v. Bl., § 70, 2), Lk 7:43.†

ὑπομονή.as:
ὑπο-μονή, -ῆς, ἡ
(ὑπομένω) [in LXX for מִקְוֶה and cogn. forms; freq. in IV Mac ;]
1.a remaining behind (Arist.).
2.patient enduring, endurance: Lk 8:1521:19, Ro 5:3, 415:4, 5, II Co 6:412:12, Col 1:11, II Th 1:4, I Ti 6:11, II Ti 3:10, Tit 2:2, He 10:36, Ja 1:3, 45:11, II Pe 1:6, Re 2:2, 3, 1913:1014:12; δι’ ὑπομονῆς, Ro 8:25, He 12:1; c. gen. pers., II Th 3:5 (ICC, in l.), Re 3:10; c. gen. rei, Ro 2:7, II Co 1:6, I Th 1:3; seq. ἐν, Re 1:9.†
SYN.: v.s. μακροθυμία, and cf. Hort on Ja 1:3

ὑποδέχομαι.long: I receive as a guest, entertain hospitably, welcome.
ὑποδέχομαι.sd: to admit under one's roof, i.e. entertain hospitably
ὑποδέχομαι.as:
** ὑπο-δέχομαι
[in LXX: To 7:8, 9, Jth 13:13 A, I Mac 16:15, IV Mac 13:17 * ;]
to receive under one's roof, receive as a guest, entertain hospitably: c. acc pers., Lk 19:6, Ac 17:7, Ja 2:25; εἰς τ. οἶκον, Lk 10:38 (v. MM, xxv).†

ὑδρωπικός.der: from a compound of G5204 (ὕδωρ) and a derivative of G3700 (ὀπτάνομαι) (as if looking watery);
ὑδρωπικός.as:
* ὑδρωπικός, -ή, -όν
(ὕδρωψ, dropsy),
dropsical, suffering from dropsy: Lk 14:2.†

ὑπωπιάζω.long: I strike under the eye, hence: I bruise, treat severely, discipline by hardship, molest, annoy, harass, worry, exhaust.
ὑπωπιάζω.sd: to hit under the eye (buffet or disable an antagonist as a pugilist), i.e. (figuratively) to tease or annoy (into compliance), subdue (one's passions)
ὑπωπιάζω.der: from a compound of G5259 (ὑπό) and a derivative of G3700 (ὀπτάνομαι);
ὑπωπιάζω.as:
* ὑπωπιάζω
(< ὑπώπιον, (a) the part of the face below the eyes; (b) a blow on the face),
to strike under the eye, give a black eye:
metaph.,
(a) of persistent annoyance (RV, wear out), Lk 18:6;
(b) of severe self-discipline (R, txt. buffet, mg. bruise), I Co 9:27 (v. Field, Notes, 71, 174).†

ὑποστρωννύω.sd: to strew underneath (the feet as a carpet)
ὑποστρωννύω.as:
ὑπο-στρωννύω
[in LXX: Is 58:5 (יצע hi.), etc. ;]
late form of ὑπο-στορέννυμι, to spread or strew under: c. acc rei, Lk 19:36.†

ὑποκρίνομαι.long: I act the part, pretend; I answer, respond.
ὑποκρίνομαι.sd: to decide (speak or act) under a false part, i.e. (figuratively) dissemble (pretend)
ὑποκρίνομαι.der: middle voice from G5259 (ὑπό) and G2919 (κρίνω);
ὑποκρίνομαι.as:
ὑπο-κρίνομαι
[in LXX: (Jb 39:32 (40:2)) אּ1 (AB אּ2ἀπο-, עָנָה), Si 1:2935 (32):15Si 36 (33):2, II Mac 5:256:21, 24, IV Mac 6:15, 17 * ;]
1. = Att.. ἀποκρίνομαι (q.v.), to answer, reply (Hom., Hdt., al.).
2.to answer on the stage, play a part (Arist., al.). Metaph., to feign, pretend (Demos., Polyb.): c. acc et inf., Lk 20:20 (cf. Ps Sol 4:22).†

ὑστέρημα.long: (a) of things or persons: that which is lacking, a defect or shortcoming, (b) want, poverty.
ὑστέρημα.kj: that which is behind, (that which was) lack(-ing), penury, want
ὑστέρημα.as:
† ὑστέρημα, -τος, τό
(< ὑστερέω), [in LXX: Jg 18:1019:19, 20, Ps 33 (34):9 (מַחְסוֹר), Ec 1:15 (חֶסְרוֹן), II Es 6:9 (ὑ. εἶναι, חֲשַׁח) * ;]
(a)that which is lacking, deficiency, shortcoming: c. gen. poss. (pron. poss.), I Co 16:17, Phl 2:30; c. gen. rei, Col 1:24, I Th 3:10;
(b)need, want, poverty (Ps 33 (34):10, Jg 18:10, al.): Lk 21:4, II Co 9:1211:9; opp. to περίσσευμα, II Co 8:13, 14 (eccl.).†

ὑπομιμνῄσκω.long: I remind; pass: I remember, call to mind.
ὑπομιμνῄσκω.sd: to remind quietly, i.e. suggest to the (middle voice, one's own) memory
ὑπομιμνῄσκω.kj: put in mind, remember, bring to (put in) remembrance
ὑπομιμνῄσκω.as:
ὑπο-μιμνήσκω
[in LXX: III Ki 4:3 B ( hi.), Wi 12:118:22, IV Mac 18:14 * ;]
to cause one to remember, put one in mind or remind one of: c. acc rei, II Ti 2:14, III Jo 10; c. dupl. acc (Thus., al.), Jo 14:26; c. acc pers., seq. περί, II Pe 1:12; id., seq. ὅτι, Ju 5; c. inf., Tit 3:1; pass., c. gen. rei, Lk 22:61.†

ὑγρός.sd: wet (as if with rain), i.e. (by implication) sappy (fresh)
ὑγρός.as:
ὑγρός, -ά, -όν,
[in LXX: Jg 16:7, 8 (לַח), Jb 8:16 (‮רָטֹב), Si 39:13אA *;]
wet, moist, opp. to ξηρός: of wood, sappy, green: Lk 23:31.†

ὑδρία.sd: a water-jar, i.e. receptacle for family supply
ὑδρία.as:
ὑδρία, -ας, ἠ
(< ὕδωρ), [in LXX for כַּד ;]
1. prop., a water-pot or jar: Jo 2:6, 74:28.
2. More freq. in Attic = ἄγγος, a pot, urn or jar of any kind, as for holding wine, coins, etc. (v. Rutherford, NPhr., 23; MM, xxv).†

ὑπόδειγμα.long: (a) a figure, copy, (b) an example, model.
ὑπόδειγμα.sd: an exhibit for imitation or warning (figuratively, specimen, adumbration)
ὑπόδειγμα.as:
ὑπό-δειγμα, -τος, τό
(< ὑποδείκνυμι), [in LXX: Ez 42:15, Si 44:16, II Mac 6:28, 31, IV Mac 17:23 * ;]
used by later writers (Xen. onwards) for παράδειγμα (v. Rutherford, NPhr., 62),
(a)a figure, copy: He 8:59:23;
(b) an example for imitation, Jo 13:15, Ja 5:10; for warning, He 4:11, II Pe 2:6.†
SYN.: ὁμοίωμα, τύπος, ὑποτύπωσις (v. DB, iii. 696b)

ὑφαντός.as:
ὑφαντός, -ή, -όν
(< ὑφαίνω), [in LXX chiefly for חָשַׁב ;]
woven: Jo 19:23.†

ὕσσωπος.long: hyssop, a stalk or stem of hyssop.
ὕσσωπος.as:
† ὕσσωπος, -ου, ἡ
[in LXX for אֵזוֹב ;]
hyssop, of which a bunch was used in ritual sprinklings: He 9:19; of a branch or rod (?) of hyssop, Jo 19:29 (but v. Field, Notes, 106 ff., for suggestion to substitute ὑσσῷ here).†

ὑπερῷον.long: an upper room, the upper part of a house.
ὑπερῷον.sd: a higher part of the house, i.e. apartment in the third story
ὑπερῷον.der: neuter of a derivative of G5228 (ὑπέρ);
ὑπερῷον.as:
ὑπερῷον, -ου, τό
(neut. of ὑπερῷος, above, < ὑπέρ) [in LXX for עֲלִיָּה and cogn. forms ;]
1. in cl., the upper story or upper rooms where the women resided (Hom., a1.).
2. In LXX and NT, an upper chamber, roof-chamber, built on the flat roof of the house (v. DB, iii, 674a): Ac 1:139:37, 3920:8 (cf. IV Ki 23:22).†

ὕπαρξις.sd: existency or proprietorship, i.e. (concretely) property, wealth
ὕπαρξις.as:
ὕπαρξις, -εως, ἡ
(< ὑπάρχω), [in LXX for רְכוּשׁ, הוֹן, etc. ;]
1.subsistence, existence (Arist., al.).
2. In late writers, = τὰ ὑπάρχοντα, substance, property: He 10:34; pl., Ac 2:45.†

ὑποβάλλω.long: I throw or put under; met: I subject, submit, suggest, whisper, prompt, suborn, instigate.
ὑποβάλλω.sd: to throw in stealthily, i.e. introduce by collusion
ὑποβάλλω.as:
** ὑπο-βάλλω
[in LXX: Da TH 3:9 A, I Es 2:18 * ;]
to throw or put under. Metaph.,
(a)to subject, submit;
(b)to suggest, whisper, prompt;
(c)to suborn (v. Field, Notes, 113), instigate: c. acc pers., Ac 6:11.†

ὑπήκοος.as:
ὑπήκοος, -ον
(< ὑπακούω), [in LXX: Jo 17:13 (לָמַם) Pr 21:28 (שׁוֺמֵעַ), etc. ;]
giving ear, obedient, subject: Phl 2:8; c. dat. pers., Ac 7:39; εἰς πάντα, II Co 2:9.†

ὑπονοέω.sd: to think under (privately), i.e. to surmise or conjecture
ὑπονοέω.as:
** ὑπο-νοέω, -ῶ
[in LXX: Da TH 7:25 (סְבַר), To 8:16, Jth 14:14, Si 23:21 * ;]
to suspect, conjecture: Ac 25:18; c. acc et inf., Ac 13:2527:27.†

ὑπηρετέω.sd: to be a subordinate, i.e. (by implication) subserve
ὑπηρετέω.as:
** ὑπηρετέω, -ῶ
(< ὑπηρέτης) [in LXX: Wi 16:21, 24, 2519:6, Si 39:4 * ;]
prop., to serve as rower on a ship (Diod., al.). In cl. always metaph., to minister to, serve: c. dat. pers., Ac 13:3620:3424:23.†

ὑετός.as:
ὑετός, -οῦ, ὁ
(< ὕω, to rain), [in LXX chiefly for מָטָר,גֶּשֶׁם ;]
rain: Ac 14:1728:2, He 6:7, Ja 5:18, Re 11:6; ὄψιμος (q.v.), sc. ὑ., Ja 5:7.†

ὑπεροράω.long: I overlook, take no notice of, disregard.

ὑποστέλλω.long: I withdraw, draw back, keep back, shun, conceal.
ὑποστέλλω.sd: to withhold under (out of sight), i.e. (reflexively) to cower or shrink, (figuratively) to conceal (reserve)
ὑποστέλλω.as:
ὑπο-στέλλω
[in LXX: De 1:17 (גּוּר), Jb 13:8 (נָשָׂאפָּנִים), Hb 2:4 (עָפַל pu.), Hg 1:10 (כָּלָא), Ex 23:21, Wi 6:7, III Mac 5:20 * ;]
1.to draw in, let down (ἱστίον, οὐράν, etc.).
2.to draw back, withdraw: ἑαυτόν, Ga 2:12 (Polyb., al.; v. Lft., in l.). Mid., to shrink or draw back: He 10:38(LXX); seq. τοῦ, c. inf., Ac 20:27; οὐδέν, ib. 20.†

ὑποπλέω.sd: to sail under the lee of
ὑποπλέω.as:
*† ὑπο-πλέω
to sail under, i.e. under the lee of: c. acc, Ac 27:4, 7.†

ὕβρις.as:
ὕβρις, -εως, ἡ
[in LXX chiefly for גָּאוֹן and cogn. forms ;]
1.wantonness, insolence.
2. = ὕβρισμα, an act of wanton violence, an outrage, injury: II Co 12:10; metaph., of a loss by sea (Pind.), Ac 27:10, 21 (v. MM, xxv).†

ὑποπνέω.as:
* ὑπο-πνέω
1.to blow underneath (Arist.).
2.to blow gently: Ac 27:13.†

ὑποτρέχω.sd: to run under, i.e. (specially), to sail past
ὑποτρέχω.der: from G5259 (ὑπό) and G5143 (τρέχω) (including its alternate);
ὑποτρέχω.as:
* ὑπο-τρέχω
to run in under; of navigators, to run in the lee of : c. acc. (v. M, Pr., 65), Ac 27:16.†

ὑποζώννυμι.long: I under-gird, as to strengthen a ship against the waves.
ὑποζώννυμι.sd: to gird under, i.e. frap (a vessel with cables across the keel, sides and deck)
ὑποζώννυμι.as:
** ὑπο-ζώννυμι
[in LXX: II Mac 3:19 * ;]
to undergird (Hdt., al.; ὑπὸ τ. μάστους, II Mac, l.c.); of a ship, to undergird or frap: Ac 27:17 (v. DB, ext. 367a).†

ὑπακοή.sd: attentive hearkening, i.e. (by implication) compliance or submission
ὑπακοή.as:
† ὑπακοή, -ῆς, ἡ
(< ὑπακούω), [in LXX: II Ki 22:36 (עֲנָוָה); in Aq.: ib. 23:23 * ;]
obedience (opp. to παρακοή);
1. in general, absol., εἰς ὑ., Ro 6:16; c. gen. subjc., II Co 7:1510:6, Phm 21; c. gen. obj., Ro 1:5 (Lft, Notes, 246) 16:26, I Pe 1:22; τ. Χριστοῦ, II Co 10:5.
2. Of obedience to God's commands: absol., I Pe 1:2; opp. to ἁμαρτία, Ro 6:16; τέκνα ὑπακοῆς, I Pe 1:14; c. gen. subj., Ro 15:1816:19.
3. Of Christ's obedience: absol., He 5:8; c. gen. subj., Ro 5:19.
(The word is not found except in LXX, NT and eccl.).†

ὑβριστής.long: an insolent, insulting, or violent man.
ὑβριστής.as:
ὑβριστής, -οῦ, ὁ
(< ὑβρίζω), [in LXX chiefly for גֵּאֶה ;]
a violent, insolent man: Ro 1:20, I Ti 1:13 (EV, injurious).†
SYN.: ἀλαζών, ὑπερήφανος, v. Tr., Syn., § xxix.

ὑπόδικος.long: answerable to, liable to (brought under) the judgment of.
ὑπόδικος.as:
* ὑπόδικος, -ον
brought to trial, answerable to: c. dat. pers., τ. θεῷ, Ro 3:19 (v. MM, xxv).†

ὑπερπερισσεύω.long: (a) intrans: I abound exceedingly, (b) dep: I overflow.
ὑπερπερισσεύω.as:
*† ὑπερ-περισσεύω
to abound more exceedingly: Ro 5:21. Mid., in same sense (RV, overflow): c. dat. rei, II Co 7:4.†

ὕπανδρος.sd: in subjection under a man, i.e. a married woman
ὕπανδρος.as:
† ὕπανδρος, -ον
[in LXX: Nu 5:20, 29 (אִישׁתַּחַת), Pr 6:24, 29, Si 9:941:21 * ;]
under or subject to a man, married: γυνή, Ro 7:2 (Polyb., Diod., al.).†

ὑπερβολή.long: excess, surpassing excellence, preeminence; adv: exceedingly.
ὑπερβολή.sd: a throwing beyond others, i.e. (figuratively) supereminence; adverbially (with G1519 (εἰς) or G2596 (κατά)) pre- eminently
ὑπερβολή.kj: abundance, (far more) exceeding, excellency, more excellent, beyond (out of) measure
ὑπερβολή.as:
** ὑπερ-βολή, -ῆς, ἡ
(< ὑπερβάλλω), [in LXX: καθ’ ὑ., IV Mac 3:18 * ;]
a throwing beyond. Metaph., excess, superiority, excellence: II Co 4:712:7; καθ’ ὑπερβολήν, beyond measure, exceedingly, Ro 7:13, I Co 12:31, II Co 1:8, Ga 1:13; κ. ὑ. εἰς ὑ. , beyond all measure, II Co 4:17.†

υἱοθεσία.long: adoption, as a son into the divine family.
υἱοθεσία.sd: the placing as a son, i.e. adoption (figuratively, Christian sonship in respect to God)
υἱοθεσία.der: from a presumed compound of G5207 (υἱός) and a derivative of G5087 (τίθημι);
υἱοθεσία.as:
*† υἱοθεσία, -ας, ἡ
(cf. the cl. phrases, υἱὸν τίθεσθαι, θετὸς υἱός), freq. in Inscr. (v. Deiss., BS, 239), adoption of a son (or daughter); metaph., of God's relation established
(a) with Israel: Ro 9:4;
(b) with Christ­ians: Ro 8:15, Ga 4:5, Eph 1:5; of its consummation, Ro 8:23.†

ὑπερεντυγχάνω.long: I intercede for, make petition for.
ὑπερεντυγχάνω.as:
*† ὑπερ-εν-τυγχάνω
to intercede or make petition for (v. Deiss., BS, 121 f.): seq. ὑπέρ, Ro 8:26.†

ὑπερνικάω.long: I am more than conqueror, prevail mightily.
ὑπερνικάω.sd: to vanquish beyond, i.e. gain a decisive victory
ὑπερνικάω.as:
**† ὑπερ-νικάω, -ῶ
[in LXX: Da TH 6:3; in Sm.: Ps 42 (43):1 * ;]
to be more than conqueror: Ro 8:37 (eccl.).†

ὕψωμα.sd: an elevated place or thing, i.e. (abstractly) altitude, or (by implication) a barrier (figuratively)
ὕψωμα.as:
ὕψωμα, -τος, τό
[in LXX: Jb 24:24 (†), Jth 10:813:415:9 * ;]
(a)height: Ro 8:39;
(b)that which is lifted up, a barrier: II Co 10:5.†

ὑπόλειμμα.as:
ὑπό-λειμμα
(WH, -λιμμα, v. their App., 154), -τος, τό, [in LXX chiefly for שְׁאֵרִית ;]
a remnant: Ro 9:27 (Arist., al.; cf. κατάλειμμα).†

ὑπολείπω.long: I leave behind; pass: I am left surviving.
ὑπολείπω.sd: to leave under (behind), i.e. (passively) to remain (survive)
ὑπολείπω.as:
ὑπο-λείπω
[in LXX chiefly (pass.) for יָתַר ni., שָׁאַר ni. ;]
to leave remaining (Hom., Thuc., al.): pass., of survivors, Ro 11:3.†

ὑπερφρονέω.long: I have high notions, am over-proud.
ὑπερφρονέω.sd: to esteem oneself overmuch, i.e. be vain or arrogant
ὑπερφρονέω.as:
** ὑπερ-φρονέω, -ῶ
[in LXX: IV Mac 13:114:1116:2 * ;]
1.to be overproud, high-minded (Æsch.): μὴ ὑ. παρ’ ὃ δεῖ φρονεῖν (on the paranom., v. Vau., in l.), Ro 12:3.
2.to overlook, think slightly of (Thuc., Plat.).†

ὑπερέχω.sd: to hold oneself above, i.e. (figuratively) to excel; participle (as adjective, or neuter as noun) superior, superiority
ὑπερέχω.as:
ὑπερ-έχω
[in LXX: Ge 25:23 (אָמַץ), Ex 26:13 (עֲדַף), Si 36:7, al. ;]
1. trans., to hold over or above.
2. Intrans. (when a noun follows, the case is governed by the prep.; v. Bl., § 34, 1; 36, 8), to rise above, overtop; metaph.,
(a)to be superior in rank, etc.: Ro 13:1, I Pe 2:13 (cf. Wi 6:6);
(b)to be superior, excel, surpass: c. gen. (cl.; v. supr.), Phl 2:3; c. acc (cl.; v. supr.), Phl 4:7; as subst., τ. ὑπερέχον, the excel­lency, the surpassing worth, Phl 3:8.†

ὑποτίθημι.long: I put under, lay down, suggest to, put in mind.
ὑποτίθημι.sd: to place underneath, i.e. (figuratively) to hazard, (reflexively) to suggest
ὑποτίθημι.as:
ὑπο-τίθημι
[in LXX for שׂוּם, etc. ;]
to place under, lay down. Metaph., τ. τράχηλον ὑποθεῖναι, to risk one's life (v. Deiss., LAE, 119 f.): Ro 16:4; mid., to suggest: I Ti 4:6.†

ὑπεροχή.sd: prominence, i.e. (figuratively) superiority (in rank or character)
ὑπεροχή.as:
ὑπεροχή, -ῆς, ἡ
(< ὑπερέχω) [in LXX: Je 52:22 (קוֹמָה), II Mac 3:11, al. ;]
a projection, eminence, as the peak of a mountain. Metaph. (Arist.), excellence, pre-eminence: λόγου ἢ σοφίας, I Co 2:1; οἱ ἐν ὑ. (for a parallel to this phrase, v. Deiss., BS, 255, and cf. II Mac, l.c.), I Ti 2:2.†

ὑπέρακμος.long: past the bloom of youth, of full age.
ὑπέρακμος.sd: beyond the "acme", i.e. figuratively (of a daughter) past the bloom (prime) of youth
ὑπέρακμος.der: from G5228 (ὑπέρ) and the base of G188 (ἀκμήν);
ὑπέρακμος.as:
*† ὑπέρακμος, -ον
past the bloom of youth: I Co 7:36 (Eustath.).†

ὑποφέρω.long: I bear up under, endure, suffer.
ὑποφέρω.sd: to bear from underneath, i.e. (figuratively) to undergo hardship
ὑποφέρω.as:
ὑπο-φέρω
[in LXX for נָשָׂא, etc. ;]
to bear by being under. Metaph., to endure: c. acc rei, I Co 10:13, II Ti 3:11, I Pe 2:19.†

ὑπερβάλλω.sd: to throw beyod the usual mark, i.e. (figuratively) to surpass (only active participle supereminent)
ὑπερβάλλω.as:
ὑπερ-βάλλω
[in LXX: Jb 15:11 A (†), Si 5:725:11, al. ;]
1. trans., to throw over or beyond.
2. Intrans., to run beyond. In both senses, metaph., to exceed, surpass, transcend: II Co 3:109:14, Eph 1:192:7; c. gen. obj., Eph 3:19.†

ὑπόστασις.long: (lit: an underlying), (a) confidence, assurance, (b) a giving substance (or reality) to, or a guaranteeing, (c) substance, reality.
ὑπόστασις.sd: a setting under (support), i.e. (figuratively) concretely, essence, or abstractly, assurance (objectively or subjectively)
ὑπόστασις.der: from a compound of G5259 (ὑπό) and G2476 (ἵστημι);
ὑπόστασις.as:
ὑπό-στασις, -εως, ἡ
(< ὑφίστημι, to set under, stand under, support) [in LXX for מַצָּב (I Ki 13:2314:4 B), תִּקְוָה (Ru 1:12, Ez 19:5), etc., also in Wi 16:21 ;]
1.a support, base or foundation (in various senses).
2.substance (Arist., al.; opp. to φαντασία, ἔμφασις): He 1:3
3.steadiness, firmness (Polyb., al.), hence, assurance, confidence: II Co 9:411:17, He 3:1411:1 (here perhaps title-deed, as that which gives reality or guarantee; v. MM, xxv).†

ὑποταγή.as:
** ὑπο-ταγή, -ῆς, ἡ
[in LXX: Wi 18:16 A * ;]
subjection: II Co 9:13, Ga 2:5. I Ti 2:113:4.†

ὑπερεκτείνω.long: I over-stretch, stretch out beyond the measure assigned to me.
ὑπερεκτείνω.as:
*† ὑπερ-εκ-τείνω
to stretch out overmuch: metaph., ἑαυτούς, II Co 10:14.†

ὑπερέκεινα.sd: above those parts, i.e. still farther
ὑπερέκεινα.der: from G5228 (ὑπέρ) and the neuter plural of G1565 (ἐκεῖνος);
ὑπερέκεινα.as:
*† ὑπερ-έκεινα
comp. adv. (v. Bl., 28, 2; M, Pr., 99),
beyond: as prep. c. gen., τὰ ὑ. ὑμῶν, II Co 10:16 (Byz. and eccl.).†

ὑπερλίαν.as:
*† ὑπερλίαν (Rec. ὑπὲρ λίαν, v. WM, § 50, 7n; B1., § 4, 1),
adv.,
exceedingly, pre-eminently: II Co 11:512:11.†

ὑπερβαλλόντως.der: adverb from present participle active of G5235 (ὑπερβάλλω);
ὑπερβαλλόντως.as:
ὑπερβαλλόντως
[in LXX: Jb 15:11א B (†) * ;]
above measure: II Co 11:23.†

ὑπεραίρομαι.long: lit: I raise beyond, uplift; mid: I lift myself up, exalt myself, am arrogant.
ὑπεραίρομαι.sd: to raise oneself over, i.e. (figuratively) to become haughty
ὑπεραίρομαι.kj: exalt self, be exalted above measure
ὑπεραίρομαι.der: middle voice from G5228 (ὑπέρ) and G142 (αἴρω);
ὑπεραίρομαι.as:
ὑπερ-αίρω
[in LXX: II Ch 32:23 (נָשָׂא ni.), etc. ;]
to lift or raise over. Mid., to uplift oneself: II Co 12:7; seq. ἐπί, c. acc, pers., II Th 2:4 (cf. II Mac 5:23).†

ὑπεράνω.sd: above upward, i.e. greatly higher (in place or rank)
ὑπεράνω.as:
ὑπερ-άνω
compound adv.,
[in LXX for עַל, מֵעָל, etc. ;]
above: as prep. c. gen., Eph 1:214:10, He 9:5.†

ὑπερεκπερισσοῦ.as:
*† ὑπερ-εκ-περισσοῦ,
comp. adv. (v. supr.),
superabundantly, exceeding abundantly: I Th 3:105:13; seq ὑπέρ, Eph 3:20 (not elsewhere).†

ὕμνος.long: a hymn, sacred song, song of praise to God.
ὕμνος.sd: probably akin to G103 (ᾄδω); compare H05667); a "hymn" or religious ode (one of the Psalms)
ὕμνος.der: apparently from a simpler (obsolete) form of (to celebrate;
ὕμνος.as:
ὕμνος, -ου, ὁ
[in LXX for תְּהִלָּה, נְגִינָה, שִׁיר, etc. ;]
a hymn;
(a) in cl. a festal song in praise of gods or heroes;
(b) in LXX and NT a song of praise addressed to God: Eph 5:19, Col 3:16.†
SYN.: ψαλμός, that which is sung to a musical accompaniment; ᾠδή, the generic term for song (cf. Tr., Syn., § lxxviii, Lft. on Col 3:16)

ὑπερυψόω.sd: to elevate above others, i.e. raise to the highest position
ὑπερυψόω.as:
† ὑπερ-υψόω, -ῶ
[in LXX: Ps 36 (37):35 (עָרִיץ) Ps 96 (97):9 (עָלָה ni.), Da TH 4:3411:12 (רוּם), ib. LXX TH 3:52ff.* ;]
1.to exalt beyond measure, exalt to the highest place: Phl 2:9.
2.to extol (Da, ll. c.).†

ὑπεναντίος.long: opposite to, adverse; subst: an adversary.
ὑπεναντίος.sd: under (covertly) contrary to, i.e. opposed or (as noun) an opponent
ὑπεναντίος.as:
ὑπ-εναντίος, -α, -ον
[in LXX for אָיַב, צַר, etc. ;]
set over against, opposite. Metaph. (Plat., Arist., al.), opposed to, contrary to: c. dat. pers., Col 2:14; absol., as subst., ὁ ὑ., He 10:27 (cf. Is 26:11).†

ὑπερβαίνω.long: I transgress; I go beyond, overreach, defraud.
ὑπερβαίνω.der: from G5228 (ὑπέρ) and the base of G939 (βάσις);
ὑπερβαίνω.as:
ὑπερ-βαίνω
[in LXX for עָבַר, etc. ;]
1. trans., to step over, trans­gress (R, overreach: I Th 4:6).
2. Intrans., to transgress: metaph., I Th 4:6 (R, txt.; v. M, Th., in l.).†

ὑπεραυξάνω.long: I increase exceedingly or beyond measure.
ὑπεραυξάνω.as:
* ὑπερ-αυξάνω
to increase beyond measure: II Th 1:3 (v. Lft., Notes, 98).†

ὑπερπλεονάζω.long: I abound exceedingly, am exceedingly abundant.
ὑπερπλεονάζω.as:
*† ὑπερ-πλεονάζω
to abound exceedingly: I Ti 1:14 (Ps Sol 5:19; Herm., Mand., v, 2, 5).†

ὑποτύπωσις.long: a pattern, example; a form, sample.
ὑποτύπωσις.sd: typification under (after), i.e. (concretely) a sketch (figuratively) for imitation
ὑποτύπωσις.der: from a compound of G5259 (ὑπό) and a derivative of G5179 (τύπος);
ὑποτύπωσις.as:
*† ὑπο-τύπωσις, -εως, ἡ
(< ὑποτυπόω, to delineate),
an outline, sketch. Metaph., a pattern, example: I Ti 1:16, II Ti 1:13.†
SYN.: ὁμοίωμα, τύπος, ὑπόδειγμα (v. DB, iii, 696b)

Ὑμέναιος.as:
Ὑμέναιος, -ου, ὁ
Hymenæus: I Ti 1:20, II Ti 2:17.†

ὑδροποτέω.long: I am only a water drinker.
ὑδροποτέω.sd: to be a water-drinker, i.e. to abstain from vinous beverages
ὑδροποτέω.der: from a compound of G5204 (ὕδωρ) and a derivative of G4095 (πίνω);
ὑδροποτέω.as:
ὑδροποτίω, -ῶ
(< ὕδωρ, πίνω), [in LXX: Da LXX 1:12שָׁתָהמַיִם) * ;]
to drink water, opp. to οἴνῳ χρῆσθαι: I Ti 5:23 (Hdt., i, 71; Plat., Rep., 561 c, al.).†

ὑπόνοια.as:
ὑπόνοια, -ας, ἡ
(< ὑπονοέω), [in LXX: Da LXX 4:16, 325:6 (רַעְיוֹן), Sir 3:34* ;]
a suspicion: I Ti 6:4.†

ὑψηλοφρονέω.sd: to be lofty in mind, i.e. arrogant
ὑψηλοφρονέω.der: from a compound of G5308 (ὑψηλός) and G5424 (φρήν);
ὑψηλοφρονέω.as:
*† ὑψηλο- φρονέω, -ῶ
= μεγαλοφρονεῖν (Xen., Plat., al.),
to be high-minded: I Ti 6:17 (WH, mg., ὑψηλὰ, φρονεῖν).†

ὑπόμνησις.long: remembrance, recollection, putting in mind; a reminder.
ὑπόμνησις.as:
ὑπό-μνησις, -εως, ἡ
(ὑπομιμνήσκω) [in LXX: Ps 70 (71):6א (תְּהִלָּה), Wi 16:11, II Mac 6:17 * ;]
a reminding, reminder: ἐν ὑ., II Pe 1:133:1; c. gen., II Ti 1:5.†

ὑποστολή.as:
*† ὑπο-στολή, -ῆς, ἡ
(< ὑποστέλλω),
1.a letting down, lowering (Plut.).
2.a shrinking back (Hesych.): οὐκ ἐσμὲν ὑποστολῆς (on the gen., v. Bl., § 35, 2), He 10:39.†

ὑπείκω.as:
** ὑπ-είκω
[in LXX: IV Mac 6:35 * ;]
1.o retire, withdraw.
2.to yield, submit: metaph., He 13:17.†

ὕλη.as:
ὕλη, -ης, ἡ
[in LXX: Jb 19:29 (†) 38:40 (סֻכָּה), Ps 68 (69):2 Blא(יָוֵן), Is 10:17 (שָׁמִיר), Wi 11:1715:13, Si 28:10, II Mac 2:24, IV Mac 1:29 * ;]
1.wood, forest, woodland (Thuc., Xen., al.).
2.wood, timber, fuel (Hom., Hdt., Thuc., al.): Ja 3:5 (v. Hort, Ja., 70, 104 f.).
3. = Lat. materia, esp. in Philosophy, matter (Arist. and later writers; Wi, ll. c.).†

ὑπογραμμός.sd: an underwriting, i.e. copy for imitation (figuratively)
ὑπογραμμός.der: from a compound of G5259 (ὑπό) and G1125 (γράφω);
ὑπογραμμός.as:
**† ὑπογραμμός, -οῦ, ὁ
(< ὑπογράφω, (a) to write under; (b) to trace letters for copying), [in LXX: II Mac 2:28 * ;]
1.a writing-copy, hence,
2.an example: I Pe 2:11 (Philo).†

ὑπέρογκος.as:
ὑπέρ-ογκος, -ον
[in LXX: De 30:11 (נִפְלֵאת), etc. ;]
of excessive weight or size; metaph., excessive, immoderate, in late writers, of arrogant speech (v. Mayor on Ju, l.c.): n. pl., II Pe 2:18, Ju 16.†

ὗς.as:
ὗς, ὑός, ὁ, ἡ
[in LXX for חֲזִיר ;]
swine: fem. (sow), II Pe 2:22,†

ὑπέχω.sd: to hold oneself under, i.e. endure with patience
ὑπέχω.as:
ὑπ-έχω
[in LXX: Ps 88 (89):50 (נָשָׂא), La 5:7 (סָבַל), Wi 12:21, II Mac 4:48 * ;]
to hold or put under. Metaph., to undergo, suffer: δίκην, Ju 7 (Soph., Eur., al.).†

ὑάλινος.as:
* ὑάλινος, -η, -ον
(< ὕαλος),
of glass, glassyRe 4:615:2.†

ὑακίνθινος.long: dark purple or blue, of the color of hyacinth.
ὑακίνθινος.as:
ὑακίνθινος, -η, -ον
(< ὑάκινθος), [in LXX for תַּחַשׁ, תְּכֵלֶת ;]
of hyacinth, hyacinthine (v.s. ὑάκινθος), "doubtless meant to describe the blue smoke of a sulphurous flame" (Swete): Re 9:17 (Hom., Eur., al.).†

ὕαλος.der: perhaps from the same as G5205 (ὑετός) (as being transparent like rain);
ὕαλος.as:
ὕαλος, -ου, ὁ
[in LXX: Jb 28:17 (זְכוּכִית) * ;]
1. (Hdt.) a clear transparent stone.
2. (from Plat. on) glass: Re 21:18, 21.†

ὑάκινθος.long: jacinth, a precious stone of the color of hyacinth.
ὑάκινθος.sd: the "hyacinth" or "jacinth", i.e. some gem of a deep blue color, probably the zirkon
ὑάκινθος.as:
ὑακίνθος, -ου, ό
[in LXX chiefly for תְּכֵלֶת ;]
hyacinth;
(a) in cl., a flower, prob. the dark blue iris;
(b) in late writers, a precious stone of the same colour, perhaps the sapphire: Re 21:20 (Phil., FlJ, al.).†
